en.headline: Chan says Hong Kong may record strongest growth in five years
en.dek: The financial secretary said first-half growth of 5.1 per cent and continued momentum into the third quarter could make 2026 the strongest full-year figure in five years.
body: Financial Secretary Paul Chan said Hong Kong could record its strongest full-year economic growth in five years in 2026, citing solid performance in the first half and into the third quarter.

Speaking on a radio programme on Saturday, Chan noted that the economy grew by 5.1 per cent in the first half of the year, with strong export performance and investment growth continuing into the third quarter. He highlighted high visitor numbers, busy streets and mega events such as the Wine and Dine Festival.

Chan said there was a chance that 2026 would mark the strongest full-year growth in the past five years. On next year's budget, he said any relief measures would depend on economic performance, while substantial infrastructure spending ahead meant public finances would need to be managed closely.

He also flagged external risks, including potential oil price rises from geopolitical tensions and the Middle East conflict, which could feed into inflationary pressures. Chan expects interest rates to stay relatively high next year, which could affect the property market and the wider economy.

zh.headline: 陳茂波：香港今年經濟增長或為五年來最強
zh.dek: 財政司司長指上半年增長5.1%，第三季勢頭持續，有機會令2026年全年增長成為過去五年最強。
body: 財政司司長陳茂波表示，香港有機會在2026年錄得五年來最強的全年經濟增長，他引述上半年的穩健表現以及第三季的持續勢頭。
陳茂波周六在電台節目中指出，上半年經濟增長5.1%，出口表現強勁及投資增長延續至第三季。他提到訪港旅客人數高、街頭繁忙，以及美酒佳餚巡禮等大型活動。
他說，2026年有機會成為過去五年來全年增長最強的一年。對於明年財政預算，他表示任何紓困措施將視乎經濟表現，而未來大量基建開支意味公共財政需要嚴密管理。
他亦提及外部風險，包括地緣政治緊張及中東衝突可能推高油價，進而帶來通脹壓力。陳茂波預期明年利率仍會相對高企，可能影響樓市及整體經濟。
